result.Method of Attack: Malicious code in preinstall scripts triggers download and execution of remote malicious scripts during package installation; downloads and runs a mining service executable named 'jsextension' from a remote IP; on Windows additionally downloads a trojan component; modification of package.json scripts field to execute malicious preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, and prenstall.sh
result.Impacted Systems: Node.js ecosystem packages depending on ua-parser-js; approximately 780 packages with 17087 versions directly dependent on ua-parser-js@0.7.28; up to 110750 versions including indirect dependencies
result.Attack Vector: Compromise of maintainer account (password leak or brute force) to publish malicious versions; supply chain attack via npm package repository
result.Indicators of Compromise: http://159.148.186.228/download/jsextension; files: preinstall.js, preinstall.bat, prenstall.sh; malicious versions: 0.7.29, 0.8.0, 1.0.0
